SV-258179.plain: Audit the six extended-attribute syscalls for both b32 and b64, for root logins and human-user logins with a set audit user ID. The manual procedure inspects loaded rules; the automated source inspects /etc/audit/audit.rules.
SV-258179.baseline: Seven Definitions ultimately AND 24 textfilecontent54 Tests. Six syscall groups have four branches each. Objects select pattern matches in the persisted file. Seventeen Variables hold regex fragments or concatenations. There are two pattern grammars and mixed Test existence modes (all/some). No States, external Variables, Sets or Filters. Collection flags and per-Object matching behavior remain observable; matching text is not evidence that the rule was loaded.
SV-258179.finding: The Tests titled b64 root lsetxattr and removexattr use b32 patterns, duplicating their b32 branches. A table must retain these anomalies for faithful comparison, not silently generate a corrected 2×2×6 matrix. Source uses regex spelling/ordering restrictions; a semantic audit parser deliberately accepts some strings the regex rejects.
SV-258179.alternatives: A: four authored regex templates plus 24 explicit rows, expanded before execution into existing independent.textfilecontent54 Tests. This is tooling, not a new runtime language. B: linux.audit_rules records with action, arch, syscall set and auid predicates; native acquisition separately names persisted and loaded snapshots. B is a collector/policy-coverage proposal, not an equivalent conversion.
SV-258179.counterexamples: Loaded missing while persisted complete; b64 root absent for lsetxattr/removexattr; reordered -F fields; split versus combined syscall lists; commented rule; unset/-1/4294967295; unknown extra success filter; unreadable file; duplicate matches; incomplete query. Parser SHALL return unsupported/unknown for conditions whose meaning it cannot establish, not ignore them.
SV-258179.cost: Template expansion has no collector change and modest authoring benefit, but regex semantics remain difficult. Parsed audit acquisition is high cost: architecture-specific syscall mapping, rule ordering, exclude/never rules, persisted includes and kernel state are unimplemented. No arbitrary command input.

SV-214228.plain: Require explicit KeepAlive On and explicit MaxKeepAliveRequests of at least 100 in the checked configuration. The threshold follows Check Text even though the title describes simultaneous session limits; KeepAlive requests concern requests per connection.
SV-214228.baseline: Four Tests AND main/config/include and loaded-config predicates: required KeepAlive On and numeric MaxKeepAliveRequests>=100 for the first group, optional occurrences constrained for loaded files. Nine Objects and eighteen Variables discover process command paths, query apachectl -V, extract roots/config names, concatenate all value combinations, grep Include/IncludeOptional, merge paths, and query loaded file lists. Shell Objects suppress nonzero-exit/stderr errors. Four States test stdout. No Sets/Filters/external Variables.
SV-214228.finding: Independent root and relative config arrays can form a Cartesian product when two installations exist. Joining by installation changes the acquired scope and needs proof rather than automatic replacement. All-occurrence policy differs from effective last-directive/default policy; grepping nested includes is not an Apache interpreter. Paths from target data enter unquoted command strings.
SV-214228.alternatives: A: shared typed acquisition of explicit directive occurrences, preserving the two source acquisition groups and four Tests. Reader still sees which group is required or optional. B: apache.configuration records keyed by installation/context, distinguishing explicit occurrences from effective values. B needs an Apache-version interpreter; effective values alone cannot implement explicit-presence requirements.
SV-214228.counterexamples: Two installations with different roots; absent explicit directives with favorable defaults; Off then On; MaxKeepAliveRequests 99/100/101/0; a VirtualHost override; nested/optional missing include; unreadable include; spaces in paths; no matching processes; nonzero command with partial stdout. The executable model isolates directive predicates, not these acquisition behaviors.
SV-214228.cost: Shared acquisition can remove repeated shell construction; scanner cost high for scope/order/include correctness. Preserve source explicitness and acquisition failure policy in a faithful mode. Default/error repairs require distinct assessment identity.

SV-257889.plain: Local initialization files must not grant forbidden group/other or special permission bits. Source selects users with UID>=1000 and users with UID<=0, excludes home /, then selects non-directory dot files one level below each home. Policy/manual uses a different /home,/root traversal example.
SV-257889.baseline: Two Definitions AND two unix.file Tests. Five Objects include a shared unix.password selection, two one-operand complement Sets with exclude Filters (UID/home), and two file selections with directory-exclude Filters. Two Variables project home_dir. Five States include eight forbidden permission booleans. The non-system Test permits empty collections; the root Test requires at least one. File recursion follows symlinks, depth 1; effective filesystem defaults are evidence, not permission to substitute local exclusions.
SV-257889.finding: A numeric mode<=0740 is incorrect: 0604 is numerically lower but grants other-read. Generic collapse of both Tests changes root missing-file behavior. The legacy complement has one operand; preserve checked-in importer handling and raise its portability ambiguity, rather than invent a second operand. Native clean-break permission booleans already solve most comparison readability.
SV-257889.alternatives: A: existing Variables, named account Objects, native downward file selection and descriptive permission booleans; retain root/non-system quantifiers. B: an authoring library for account-home file selection expanded to the same graph, leaving all traversal choices explicit. No new permission test or mode field is justified.
SV-257889.counterexamples: UID999/1000; UID0 and home /; zero normal-user files versus zero root files; mode0604,0740,0700,04740; symlink loop, local/remote mount transition, unreadable home; directory dot entry excluded; duplicate home paths. Synthetic bit tests prove comparison only, not traversal equivalence.
SV-257889.cost: Existing capability composition: low language cost, meaningful naming benefit. Traversal implementation remains high and belongs to scanner. Shell find is rejected. Source filesystem semantics cannot silently be changed to local-only while calling conversion faithful.

SV-258236.plain: Crypto policy must match generated policy and back-end links must target FIPS files, with nss.config a regular file. Operational subpolicy exceptions need AO/ISSO documentation; they are not permission for an input to bypass Tests.
SV-258236.baseline: Two Definitions AND twelve Tests/Objects/States: eleven unix.symlink canonical-target equalities and one unix.file type=regular check for nss. No Variables, Sets, Filters or external inputs. Every selected resource must exist.
SV-258236.finding: The source checks twelve back ends but manual text also displays openssl_fips and asks update-crypto-policies --check. Source does not prove configured/generated content equality merely by canonical paths. Preserve literal target equality; do not assume textual symlink target equals canonical resolved target.
SV-258236.alternatives: A: a finite required-row table expanded to eleven ordinary symlink Tests and one ordinary file Test; no new collector. B: focused update-crypto-policies --check command in addition to native links, under a documented utility/exit/output contract. B improves policy coverage but is not lossless.
SV-258236.counterexamples: One missing backend; wrong target; broken link; relative target resolving correctly; nss symlink versus regular file; all links correct but policy content altered; newly added backend; incomplete collection. Table duplicates require rejection; evidence capping cannot omit failed rows.
SV-258236.cost: Low authoring-tool cost and no runtime invention for A. B requires utility/version behavior evidence, privilege and locale; not implemented or executed. Both retain native filesystem acquisition.

SV-278028.plain: For installed FTP sites, keep shared resources away from drive roots, Program Files and Windows system areas. FTP absence is applicability, not a configuration pass inferred from a failed query.
SV-278028.baseline: Four Tests require no reported prohibited-directory matches. Nine Objects use appcmd FTP bindings, site-name-derived Get-Website commands and environmentvariable58 system-area paths. Eight Variables build queries/patterns; five States filter binding records or compare output. Applicability includes a separate FTP-installed Assessment. No Sets or external Variables.
SV-278028.finding: Constructing Get-Website 'site-name' via concat is not safe argument binding. Empty output can mean no prohibited matches, no sites or swallowed failure. A textual prefix does not establish resolved directory containment or junction traversal.
SV-278028.alternatives: A: bounded structured IIS query returning site ID/bindings/physicalPath records, then native path comparisons with constrained environment paths. B: typed IIS site collector, identity-preserving variable expansion and a native path-relation predicate. B must distinguish configured path from resolved filesystem target.
SV-278028.counterexamples: No FTP; two sites one bad; a quote in site name; environment expansion; C:\WindowsOld versus C:\Windows; drive root; inaccessible site configuration; path junction into protected area; missing env variable. Failures SHALL NOT be empty-success records.
SV-278028.cost: Medium structured-query cost; high path/junction correctness cost belongs in native collector. Avoid general shell filesystem discovery. Organizational values cannot construct queries or choose sites.

SV-278138.plain: On domain controllers, protect AD database/log files so SYSTEM and Administrators have full rights and others have no effective rights. Domain-controller detection remains separate applicability.
SV-278138.baseline: Two Definitions; registry path discovery feeds three Variables for log path, database parent, and working directory. Twelve Objects and nine Tests repeat SYSTEM full-rights, Administrators full-rights, and no other rights for each directory. Four States define seventeen right booleans, known SIDs and no-rights. Filters remove allowed principals and zero-right rows; fileeffectiverights53 collection group/SID behaviors remain significant.
SV-278138.finding: A DACL ACE allowlist is not an effective-rights collector. Deny/allow order, inheritance, token group membership and unknown principals cannot be erased. Collapsing per-directory existence into one global some permits an empty/missing directory to hide behind another.
SV-278138.alternatives: A: finite directory×principal authoring table expanded to existing windows.fileeffectiverights53 Tests, preserving Filters and per-directory existence. B: keyed effective-right records reused by three predicates, if collection behavior and identity universe can be shown equivalent. No new effective rights semantics proposed.
SV-278138.counterexamples: Two directories one empty; non-DC; unknown SID; inherited allow plus deny; local/domain group; inaccessible registry or file; zero-right stranger filtered versus stranger with one right; directory/file distinction; junction. Synthetic ACE order test is a counterexample only, not Windows evaluator conformance.
SV-278138.cost: Low template cost, high acquisition cost already present in native effective-rights capability. A general permission Boolean hides policy and is rejected.

SV-278001.plain: Maintain restrictive registry ACLs on HKLM SECURITY, SOFTWARE and SYSTEM, with documented DC/member principal differences and the specified application-package SID exception.
SV-278001.baseline: Five Tests, four Objects, three constant regex-list Variables and five States. PowerShell formats ACE fields to strings and filters numeric RegistryRights displays before regex comparison. WMI DomainRole records distinguish 4/5 from other roles. Every returned ACE string must match some allowed pattern; this is not a required-principal equality check.
SV-278001.finding: Filtering numeric-right displays can omit an ACE from assessment; English IdentityReference/enum formatting is fragile. All observed ACEs allowed does not prove every default ACE exists. Requiring a complete default table is a policy change, while switching to effective rights would change the object of review.
SV-278001.alternatives: A: typed explicit registry ACE records preserving access type/inheritance/propagation and source whitelist semantics. B: required default ACL policy comparison, separately identified as intent/coverage refinement. Retain WMI-authored platform/role facts; do not add scanner OS magic.
SV-278001.counterexamples: Allowed subset missing SYSTEM; numeric-right ACE hidden; localized principal names; DC DomainRole 4/5; role unknown; custom application SID; deny/allow ordering; null versus empty DACL; inaccessible registry. Structural ACE checks and effective access have separate contracts.
SV-278001.cost: Medium structured acquisition cost; needs generic-mask mapping and SID resolution. A typed ACE schema is clearer than regex strings but cannot claim identical behavior until representation omissions are accounted for.

SV-259350.plain: Applicable DNS zones must include RRSIG, DNSKEY and NSEC3 records; DS is checked elsewhere. Classified networks and exclusively AD-integrated zones are explicit exceptions.
SV-259350.baseline: Six Tests OR caching-only, all-forward-zones-AD-integrated, or signed+three positive record-count predicates. Seven shell Objects and four Variables discover/filter zones and invoke per-zone queries. Six States compare output; no external Variables or Sets. General config commands exclude Forwarder/TrustAnchors/autocreated zones; reverse zones are excluded from forward checks.
SV-259350.finding: The Assessment title references RRSet authorization but body tests relevant DNSSEC presence; title mismatch alone is not a logic defect. Zone identity is lost in stdout counts. Original variable instances may still preserve per-command scope: do not assert cross-zone false pass without an evaluator. Classified input/applicability is not modeled by an external Variable in this graph.
SV-259350.alternatives: A: a fixed structured per-zone administrative query with zone ID and each required RR count/status. B: native DNS record collector with the same typed records. Require per-zone completeness, not independent favorable arrays. Classification is a constrained applicability value in a separate Assessment, never command data.
SV-259350.counterexamples: Three zones each providing a different RR type; one zone query fails; unsigned zone; all AD-integrated; mixed integrated/file zones; caching-only; classified; NSEC rather than NSEC3; record-count zero; stale partial inventory. Preserve source integrated bypass separately from stronger mixed-zone policy.
SV-259350.cost: Medium batched-query collector cost; low predicate cost. One keyed record can remove four command-building Variables, but snapshot/error behavior and variable-instance equivalence remain unproved.

SV-259345.plain: For applicable zones, both KSK and ZSK DNSKEY signature validity periods must be between 48 and 168 hours inclusive. Classified and exclusively AD-integrated servers are exceptions.
SV-259345.baseline: Five Tests OR caching-only, all-forward-zones-integrated, or signed+KSK bounds+ZSK bounds. Six shell Objects, three command Variables and five States. Duration commands calculate Days*24+Hours and return 0 on caught exception. Tests aggregate both bounds across every returned value.
SV-259345.finding: Minutes/seconds are discarded: 168h+1s can compare as 168. Exact duration bounds are a behavioral refinement, not a faithful replacement. Query error encoded as zero is a failure under this source, whereas typed collector error is a different outcome.
SV-259345.alternatives: A: typed zone/key records retaining the legacy integer-hour projection and error-to-zero adapter as an explicit compatibility mode. B: exact duration predicate in seconds with separate per-key status. B is an intent refinement requiring publisher review; keep KSK and ZSK existence explicit.
SV-259345.counterexamples: 47:59:59,48h,168h,168h+1s; KSK present/ZSK missing; unsigned; one good and one bad zone; caught error produces zero versus error; all integrated; classified; empty forward set. Key type and zone identity SHALL remain attached.
SV-259345.cost: Medium query/schema cost, small comparison cost. Duration units are reusable; no generic hidden compliance collector. Actual Windows UI/cmdlet constraints might restrict sub-hour values; target reachability remains unproven.

SV-259374.plain: DNS interfaces must have configured static IPv4 addressing, prefix/subnet mask and gateway. The manual checks all adapters; source checks Status Up adapters and accepts zero online adapters.
SV-259374.baseline: Five Tests OR a Variable count==0 or four all-value command predicates. Six Objects, five Variables and three States. Get-NetAdapter ifIndex drives separate address, prefix, gateway and SuffixOrigin queries; exceptions are caught without output. Four States/Tests require nonempty per-output entities; source uses SuffixOrigin=Manual as static signal.
SV-259374.finding: A row carrying interface/address identity is safer to review than separate arrays. This does not prove the original variable-instance machinery loses correlation. PrefixOrigin/DHCP and SuffixOrigin are not automatically interchangeable. Requiring every offline adapter changes source scope.
SV-259374.alternatives: A: fixed batched query retaining source Up and SuffixOrigin policy with one record per interface/address plus gateway relation. B: typed network capability with explicit static-address facts; replacing the static signal is a separate policy decision. Existing variable.value can remove the count-wrapper Object without new language.
SV-259374.counterexamples: Zero online; one interface missing gateway; multiple IPv4 addresses; prefix0/32 versus merely nonempty; gateway on other interface; Manual suffix but DHCP facts differ; IPv6-only; offline adapter; query exception; unknown status. Explicit duplicates need an address key rather than unique ifIndex alone.
SV-259374.cost: Medium batch collector cost, low language cost with existing record State aggregation. Arbitrary joins may be unnecessary if collector returns typed related rows.

SV-214268.plain: Load session_cookie_module, enable Session, and configure session cookies with HttpOnly and Secure. Preserve the manual procedure's explicit directives; runtime flags must refer to the same cookie/context.
SV-214268.baseline: Five Tests AND required Session/cookie directives in main+include scope, optional loaded-config occurrences constrained, and module presence. Ten Objects, nineteen Variables and seven States repeat Apache discovery/include/script construction from SV-214228. Cookie Tests require both flag regexes in each Item via states_match all.
SV-214268.finding: Original Item-State aggregation already prevents two distinct cookie Items from sharing flags; do not justify a new correlation primitive with a defect the source does not have. Regex substring matching does not establish cookie attribute token boundaries; Session On substring handling is not a full scoped interpreter.
SV-214268.alternatives: A: shared Apache acquisition library plus unchanged Item-local States. B: typed directive/cookie records with case-insensitive attribute tokens and configuration scope. B adds parser semantics and can change source substring results. Reuse acquisition proposed for SV-214228, not an unrelated cookie compliance collector.
SV-214268.counterexamples: Cookie A only HttpOnly and cookie B only Secure; HttpOnlyFake token; Secure in cookie name; Session Off/On in different contexts; missing module; main absent but included present; unreadable include; multiple installations; duplicate directives. Source substring results versus tokenized results need separate expected columns.
SV-214268.cost: High shared config collector cost; moderate author benefit. Existing per-Item AND can handle fields without a new language primitive.

SV-214292.plain: Every directory below each DocumentRoot must have index.html or an equivalent default document, according to Check Text. Policy concerns directory listing/default pages, which also depends on Apache configuration.
SV-214292.baseline: Two Tests AND existence of case-insensitive index.html selections for two discovered DocumentRoot groups. Nine Objects and eighteen Variables reuse shell discovery/config/includes but file acquisition is native unix.file. No States/Filters/Sets/external Variables. No recursive file traversal behavior is explicit on those file Objects.
SV-214292.finding: The source looks for index.html at selected roots, not every descendant directory or configured equivalent default documents. Index.HTML case-insensitive match differs from Unix server lookup rules. Do not label recursive/effective DirectoryIndex/Options checking equivalent to this source.
SV-214292.alternatives: A: shared typed DocumentRoot discovery plus existing native file existence Tests. B: native per-directory traversal plus Apache DirectoryIndex/Options context; this is a coverage correction, not refactor. Directory discovery/traversal SHALL remain native, including filesystem exclusions, links and permissions.
SV-214292.counterexamples: Root index exists but child lacks one; only index.php default; Index.HTML on case-sensitive filesystem; Options -Indexes with no index; inaccessible child; remote subtree; symlink/junction; two roots one missing; no discovered roots. Scope and expected absence must be explicit.
SV-214292.cost: Moderate author-tool benefit for A. High collector/policy-interpretation cost for B. Shell recursion is rejected even though manual Check Text uses find.
